metadata.note: Two historical, now-discontinued Detroit-Flint rail corridors, researched from Wikipedia and Michigan railroad-history sites in response to a question about whether such service ever existed. Both predate any GTFS/live-data era and have no modern segment (no through Detroit-Flint passenger train has run since Amtrak's 1971 creation). Route geometry follows the real intermediate towns each railroad's own history describes, but is a simplified handful of waypoints, not surveyed track centerline. Era boundaries follow real corporate-history milestones (line openings, mergers, discontinuation dates); headway_min and avg_speed_kmh within each era are estimates, not sourced from real timetables.
metadata.source: Wikipedia, michiganrailroads.com, trains.com, american-rails.com (see conversation for citations)
metadata.line_label_audit: 2026-08-24: line labels normalised repo-wide to "<operating company>: <line name>" -- the company's common display name (legal suffixes dropped), then the line as a passenger would have known it, or its two terminals where the line carried no advertised name. Long intermediate station lists were reduced to endpoints. For features spanning several operators the company shown is the one that ran the line for most of its drawn years. See CLAUDE.md Rule 6.

segments.note: Flint & Pere Marquette's Holly, Wayne & Monroe Ry acquisition (1872) gave it its own Detroit-Plymouth-Northville-Novi-Milford-Fenton-Flint line, completed 1871, avoiding reliance on the connecting Detroit & Milwaukee route it had used via Holly since 1864. estimated era boundary/frequency; based on researched historical milestones, not a real timetable

segments.note: Chesapeake & Ohio absorbed the Pere Marquette in 1947; postwar decline in branch-line passenger service followed. C&O ended all Michigan passenger service April 30 1971, the eve of Amtrak, which did not pick up this route. estimated era boundary/frequency; based on researched historical milestones, not a real timetable

properties.line: Grand Trunk Western Railroad: Detroit-Flint (via Pontiac & Durand)

segments.note: Detroit & Milwaukee (reorganized as Detroit, Grand Haven & Milwaukee) reached Pontiac in the 1850s; the Grand Trunk's own line reached Flint from Port Huron in 1871 and Durand by 1876, completing a through Detroit-Pontiac-Durand-Flint route by around 1877. estimated era boundary/frequency; based on researched historical milestones, not a real timetable

segments.note: DGH&M formally merged into the Grand Trunk Western in 1928. GTW's Detroit-Flint-Saginaw-Bay City steam passenger service made its last run Sept 20 1961, one of the last regularly scheduled steam passenger operations in the US. estimated era boundary/frequency; based on researched historical milestones, not a real timetable
